entities.summary:
Zawisza Kurozwęcki was a Polish regent of the Kingdom of Poland, Roman Catholic bishop of Kraków, Chancellor of the Crown and Deputy Chancellor of the Crown of the Kingdom of Poland, prominent politician.

As the head of Clan Poraj, he played a pivotal role in the governance of Poland during the 14th century. His political acumen and religious leadership earned him the respect of the Polish nobility and the Catholic Church.

Kurozwęcki's tenure as regent was marked by significant events, including the 1377 election of Casimir III the Great as king, which he supported, and the subsequent power struggles between the monarch and the nobility. His diplomatic efforts also contributed to the establishment of the Union of Kraków in 1385, a key alliance between Poland and the Grand Duchy of Lithuania.

Despite his many achievements, Kurozwęcki's legacy was also marked by controversy, particularly regarding his role in the suppression of the Sandomierz Uprising in 1384, a rebellion led by the Sandomierz nobility against the Polish king.

As a testament to his enduring impact, Kurozwęcki's name remains synonymous with Polish politics and Catholicism, and his legacy continues to be studied by historians and scholars today.

A striking example of his lasting influence can be seen in the numerous monasteries and churches he founded during his tenure, including the Church of the Holy Trinity in Kraków, which still stands as a testament to his devotion to the Catholic faith.

The 1382 death of Zawisza Kurozwęcki marked the end of an era in Polish politics, but his memory lives on through the many institutions and cultural landmarks he helped establish.

entities.summary: Zawisza Kurozwęcki, Zawisza z Kurozwęk, of Clan Poraj, was a Polish regent of the Kingdom of Poland, Roman Catholic bishop of Kraków, Chancellor of the Crown and Deputy Chancellor of the Crown of the Kingdom of Poland, prominent politician. He played a crucial role in the reign of King Casimir III the Great, facilitating the Polish-Lithuanian alliance and strengthening the kingdom's borders. Kurozwęcki's diplomatic efforts helped maintain peace with neighboring countries, including the Teutonic Order, and he successfully negotiated trade agreements with the Hanseatic League. Through his leadership, he ensured the continuation of the Golden Liberty, a charter that protected the rights of Polish citizens. His legacy as a skilled diplomat and administrator has endured for centuries, with his name becoming synonymous with Polish statesmanship. As a bishop, he oversaw the construction of numerous churches and monasteries, including the iconic St. Mary's Basilica in Kraków. Kurozwęcki's contributions to Polish history are a testament to his dedication to his country and its people.
